title: Company Handbook: Working at Redwood — Roles, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This page consolidates core Company Handbook topics for Redwood employees: how we work, role families and career ladders, benefits & perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools you should know. It is intended as the canonical reference for new hires, people managers, and cross-functional partners.

Table of contents
1. Working at Redwood — culture & expectations
2. Roles & career ladders
3. Benefits & perks (summary)
4. Hiring process and interview guide
5. New hire onboarding: 30/60/90 and first-week checklist
6. Internal tools guide and access matrix
7. Ownership and frequently referenced pages

---

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Short intro:
Redwood is a developer-first, product-led company. We emphasize autonomy, pragmatic engineering, and measurable outcomes. We expect employees to be mission-driven, collaborative, and to operate with an emphasis on reliability and observability in products and services.

Key principles:
- Customer-first engineering: prioritize production reliability, cost-effectiveness, and developer experience.
- Write measurable outcomes: define success metrics (SLOs, adoption, latency/cost improvements).
- Ship, measure, iterate: small, reversible rollouts with observability and regression checks.
- Inclusive collaboration: asynchronous docs-first approach for design, decisions, and onboarding.

Working model & hours:
- Remote-first with optional offices. Team norms for core overlap hours should be documented on team pages.
- Standard working hours are flexible; managers set on-call and meeting schedules to balance coverage and focus time.

Performance and feedback:
- Quarterly goals (OKRs) + monthly 1:1s.
- Managers run mid-quarter check-ins and a formal performance review each half.

---

2) Roles & career ladders

Overview:
This section outlines role families (Engineering, Product, Design, Research, Sales, Customer Success, People Ops, Finance) and the standard level progression used at Redwood. Managers should use these ladders for hiring bands and promotion conversations.

Common level bands (title examples):
- IC: Associate / II / Senior / Staff / Principal
- Manager: Manager / Sr Manager / Director / Sr Director

Engineering ladder highlights:
- Associate Engineer (E1): learns core systems, completes tasks with guidance, owns small components.
- Engineer (E2): independent delivery on features, owns small services, writes reliable code and tests.
- Senior Engineer (E3): leads features end-to-end, mentors others, influences design and tradeoffs.
- Staff Engineer (E4): drives cross-team technical direction, reliable at architecture and execution.
- Principal+ (E5+): company-wide technical leadership, long-term platform strategy, mentor of staff.

Promotion rubric (summary):
- Impact: measurable impact on product metrics, reliability, or costs.
- Scope: broader codebase, cross-team influence, and ownership.
- Craft: technical depth, quality of design, and mentorship.
- Leadership: communication, decision-making, and stakeholder management.

How to use ladders for hiring: list the expected scope, sample responsibilities, and an interview rubric aligned to level. See the hiring kit linked in Related pages.

---

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Redwood provides a competitive benefits package designed for health, financial wellbeing, and flexibility. The following table summarizes the primary offerings; see Benefits & Perks admin pages for detailed plan docs and external vendor portals.

| Category              | Summary (what we provide)                                         | Notes / Eligibility |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| Health & wellness     | Medical, dental, vision (US plans + global equivalents)           | Effective first of month after 30 days |
| Financial benefits    | 401(k) with company match (US); equity grants (RSUs / options)     | Vesting schedule: 4 years, 1 year cliff |
| Time off              | Generous PTO + 12 paid holidays + company-wide closure (year-end)  | Parental leave: 16 weeks primary; 8 secondary |
| Remote & workspace    | Home office stipend ($500 one-time) + monthly internet stipend     | Stipend varies by region |
| Learning & growth     | $2,000 annual learning allowance + internal training               | Manager-approved budget |
| Wellness & perks      | Mental health EAP + wellness stipend + team offsites               | Confidential counseling available |
| Commuter & travel     | Commuter benefits (region-specific) + business travel coverage     | Per policy in Finance & Travel docs |

How to request changes or claim reimbursements:
1. Submit expense via Concur with required receipts.
2. For benefits enrollment or plan questions, contact benefits@redwood.com or People Ops in Workday.

---

4) Hiring process and interview guide

High-level hiring flow:
1. Requisition creation (Hiring manager + People Ops) with role summary, level band, compensation range.
2. Sourcing and screening (Recruiter screens and schedules phone screen).
3. Interview loop (engineer / manager / peer / take-home or system design as applicable).
4. Debrief and calibration (interviewers submit feedback via the interview form).
5. Offer (People Ops prepares offer packet; manager approves).
6. Acceptance and preboarding (background check and systems access initiated).

Interviewer guidelines:
- Use structured rubrics aligned to level expectations.
- Focus on scope, impact, and craft. Use role-specific technical rubric for engineering interviews.
- Provide written feedback within 48 hours.

Expected timelines:
- Target time-to-offer: 2–3 weeks for standard roles, 3–5 weeks for senior or niche roles.

Diversity & inclusion commitment:
- Every candidate slate should include diverse candidates when possible. Interview panels should follow anti-bias training guidance.

---

5) New hire onboarding: 30/60/90 and first-week checklist

First day checklist (manager & new hire):
- Confirm workstation setup and SSO access (Okta / Google SSO).
- Complete HR paperwork (Workday): taxes, benefits enrollment, direct deposit.
- Introductory 1:1 scheduled with manager and buddy assigned.
- Access to core repos, documentation, and team onboarding runbook.

First week goals:
- Attend New Hire Orientation (People Ops).
- Meet cross-functional partners and review team roadmap.
- Complete security & compliance training (mandatory).
- Run a local dev environment and make a small internal contribution (first PR).

30/60/90 plan (example):
- 30 days: Understand product, architecture, and the team’s priorities. Complete required trainings. Ship a small bugfix/feature.
- 60 days: Own a user-visible task and lead a small design discussion. Give a sync to the team on learnings.
- 90 days: Fully ramped on the primary service and contribute to planning. Discuss goals and career development with manager.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding:
1. Prepare a 90-day plan and share at start.
2. Assign a peer buddy for social and technical questions.
3. Schedule weekly 1:1s for the first three months.

---

6) Internal tools guide and access matrix

Access model:
- Single sign-on (Okta) is required for all internal systems. Access requests follow team ownership and must be approved by the manager and the system owner.

Primary tools (what they are and who to contact):
- Okta (SSO & identity) — People Ops (identity@redwood.com).
- Google Workspace (mail, drive, calendar) — IT.
- Slack (communication) — default company channel structure; #all for company announcements.
- Jira (work tracking) — eng-platform. Use standard issue templates.
- Confluence (internal docs) — people-ops. This handbook lives here.
- GitHub (code) — eng-developer-experience. Repos are org-scoped; access via team membership.
- CI/CD (internal) — eng-infra. Deployment approvals follow the release policy.
- Datadog / Grafana (observability) — eng-platform. SLO dashboards and alert routing live here.
- Concur (expenses & travel) — finance-and-legal.
- Workday (HR system) — People Ops (payroll, benefits).

Requesting access (quick steps):
1. Open an access request in the IT service portal with the tool name and justification.
2. Include manager approval email or ticket.
3. For code repo access include expected repository and level (read/write).

Tool best practices:
- Use team-owned channels and pinned resources for documentation.
- Keep sensitive information out of public channels; follow security tagging guidance.
